spine: Company trade -> parliamentary control -> dual control -> Crown rule -> association -> representation -> provincial responsibility -> federation/autonomy -> sovereignty

stages.title: CORPORATE STATE BEFORE 1773
must_show: Company commercial rule acquired governmental functions.
Defect: private corporation exercised public power without constitutional accountability.
Consequence: Parliament intervenes, not because Company ceased to trade.
stages.answer_band: Corporate power first produced the need for statutory control.

stages.title: REGULATING ACT 1773
must_show: Bengal presidency made supervisory centre over Bombay and Madras.
Governor-General in Council and Supreme Court created dual authorities.
Defect: jurisdictional conflict and weak central control remained.
stages.answer_band: 1773 begins regulation, but did not create a coherent central government.

stages.title: SETTLEMENT ACT 1781
must_show: Clarified Supreme Court limits over revenue administration.
Protected acts done in public/revenue capacity from ordinary court interference.
Bridge: exposed why Parliament needed a control system above ad-hoc clarification.
stages.answer_band: 1781 repaired the 1773 court–executive conflict; it did not settle political control.

stages.title: PITT'S INDIA ACT 1784
must_show: BOARD OF CONTROL: political, civil, military and revenue government.
COURT OF DIRECTORS: commercial administration retained.
Consequence: Company survived commercially; British Government gained decisive state supervision.
stages.answer_band: Pitt's Act separated commercial management from sovereign supervision.

stages.title: 1786 + CHARTER ACT 1793
must_show: 1786 strengthened Governor-General where council opposition obstructed policy.
1793 renewed monopoly without altering dual-control principle.
Direction: executive capacity and Parliamentary oversight deepened together.
stages.answer_band: The early Charter phase retained Company commerce while tightening imperial direction.

stages.title: CHARTER ACT 1813
must_show: Ended Company monopoly in Indian trade; tea/China remained excepted.
Opened India to other British merchants and missionaries.
Marked Company shift from trader toward governing agency.
stages.answer_band: 1813 weakened commercial exclusivity without yet ending Company rule.

stages.title: CHARTER ACT 1833
must_show: Centralised legislative power under Governor-General of India.
Company ceased commercial functions; remained administrative instrument.
Law Member/legislative machinery signalled uniform imperial governance.
stages.answer_band: 1833 converted the Company from trader-ruler into a governing instrument.

stages.title: CHARTER ACT 1853
must_show: Separated legislative functions of Governor-General’s Council.
Opened civil-service competition in principle.
No fixed twenty-year renewal: Company tenure became provisional.
stages.answer_band: 1853 made the Company constitutional machinery awaiting replacement.

stages.title: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1858
must_show: Company rule ended after 1857; Crown assumed government.
Secretary of State in Council replaced Board/Court control machinery.
Governor-General became Viceroy: imperial executive now directly responsible to Crown.
stages.answer_band: 1858 replaces Company governance with Crown responsibility, not representative government.

stages.title: COUNCILS ACTS 1861 + 1892
must_show: 1861 restored legislative councils and recognised portfolio administration.
1892 enlarged councils and introduced an indirect electoral principle.
Limit: executives remained unresponsible to elected Indians.
stages.answer_band: Councils widened consultation; they did not yet transfer executive responsibility.

must_show: 1909 institutionalised separate communal electorates.
1919 split provincial subjects: transferred ministers versus reserved Governor control.
Responsible government remained partial and provincial, not central.
stages.answer_band: 1909 changed representation; 1919 tested limited responsibility through dyarchy.

stages.title: GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ACT 1935
must_show: Proposed federation; federal part did not fully operate.
Federal, provincial and concurrent lists structured legislative power.
Provincial autonomy expanded, but Governors retained safeguards/discretion.
stages.answer_band: 1935 supplied the institutional grammar later adapted by the Constitution.

stages.title: INDEPENDENCE ACT 1947
must_show: Created India and Pakistan as independent Dominions.
Lapsed British paramountcy over princely states.
Constituent Assembly acquired sovereign law-making authority.
stages.answer_band: 1947 ends imperial constitutional control and opens constitution-making sovereignty.
